title: Twice the Pull? Friction Mu Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Slide an empty box: easy. Fill it with books: much harder. On ice, it glides. Aarav drags a carton of record books down the college corridor: twice the books needs twice the pull, yet standing the carton on its narrow end changes nothing. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we meet the coefficient of friction, mu.

On a live simulation a spring balance pulls a block while weights are added, so the normal force N grows from 20 to 60 newtons. The balance reading peaks at the maximum static friction, then drops to kinetic friction, and every point lands on two straight lines through zero on the friction vs N graph, with a slow-mo replay of the moment the block starts to slide. We build f_s,max = mu_s N and f_k = mu_k N step by step, see why mu has no unit and why mu_s is bigger than mu_k, and show link by link why friction does not depend on the area of contact. Then a worked example, the exam trap about f = mu_s N at rest, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Empty box, full box, box on ice
0:26 What friction depends on: N and the surfaces
0:47 The spring balance sim: friction vs N, live graph
1:32 The rule: f = mu N, step by step
2:14 Same N, different surfaces + pause and think
2:47 Why area does not matter, link by link + pause and think
3:31 Worked example: mu from balance readings
4:07 Exam trap
4:28 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:09 Recap and three questions
